review_notes: I read the whole file and checked the simp lemmas it depends on. These were `ofArrow_eq_ofPath` and the `liftAlgHomOfArrows_*` evaluation lemmas in OfArrows.lean, plus Mathlib's `Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk`. The file declares no simp lemmas of its own, and I found no missing canonical lemma, loop or competing rule there. The only issue is that the proofs pass explicit simp arguments that are already `@[simp]`. That shows the simp set is not being relied on as intended, but it does no harm, so the finding is minor. I did not run Lean, so I did not check whether removing the arguments compiles.

findings.problem: The proofs hand `simp` lemmas that are already `@[simp]`. `ofArrow_eq_ofPath` is a simp lemma. `Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk` is also `@[simp]` in Mathlib. The OfArrows docstring says `liftAlgHomOfArrows_ofPath_toPath` is 'the simp-normal form of evaluation on `ofArrow`'. So plain `simp` already evaluates `liftAlgHomOfArrows … (ofArrow a)` to `f a`. Repeating the lemma at lines 99, 110, 116 and 143 makes the reader think the simp set cannot reach these goals unaided. It also hides that the library's simp interface for `ofArrow` is complete. In the opposite direction, if the orientation of `ofArrow_eq_ofPath` ever changed, these call sites would stay silently fine while the intended normal form changed.
findings.proposed_change: Drop the redundant arguments and rely on the simp set. Line 116 becomes `by simp [F]`. Line 143 becomes `by simpa using harrows a`. Line 110 becomes `simp`. Line 99 becomes `simp [F, ← hc]`. If the `F` unfolding is only there because of the `set`, keep it. Where a call needs an explicit `liftAlgHomOfArrows_ofPath_toPath`-style fact, cite that name instead.
findings.benefit: The proofs then show which rewrites are real simp-normal-form steps and which are local unfoldings (`F`, `ψ`). This also confirms that `ofArrow` evaluation is handled by the canonical simp lemmas, and it removes noise a reader would otherwise have to check.
